newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. dlr ends weak in HK, outwatching FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dlr ends weak in HK, outwatching FOMC.

text.p: The U.S. dollar ended a quiet Hong Kong session sharply weaker against the New York close on Friday, with dealers reporting a thin and inactive market.
"At least half the market is gone," one analyst said.
Foreign exchange traders were reported to have decamped in favour of the Hong Kong Rugby Sevens World Cup.
An overnight surge on comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who gave clear signals that rates could rise as early as next week, dissipated in the Asian session.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy-making arm of the Federal Reserve, meets on March 25.
Against the mark, the dollar fell into consolidation mode after testing stop-losses at 1.6946 marks, ending the Friday session at about 1.6912/17.
Against the yen, the dollar sank after heavy selling by one major Asian central bank at a high of 123.73 to close at about 123.34.
"Dollar sentiment remains bid on the dips given the wider interest rate differentials," one analyst said.

One or two longer term players are moving back into the dollar as the market prices in expectations of a 25 basis point increase in U.S. rates next week, but with the long bond approaching a seven-percent yield, some traders questioned the need for any rate rise.
The U.S. 30-year yield closed at 6.96 percent on Thursday.
The Hong Kong dollar was trading weaker at HK$7.7483 with the currency forwards at 19 basis points in the three-month and 43 basis points in the six-month.
Overnight was at 5.06 percent. The three-month deposit was at 5.75 percent against the U.S. three-month treasury at 5.34 percent for a spread of 41 basis points.
The two-year Hong Kong Exchange Fund Note (EFN) yield was at 6.13 percent against the U.S. two-year at 6.26 percent for a spread of 13 basis points.
The 10-year EFN yield was at 7.39 percent against the U.S. 10-year at 6.73 percent for a spread of 66 basis points.
Among other yields, the three-year was at 6.45 percent, the five-year was at 6.97 percent, the seven-year was at 7.17 percent and the one-week was at 5.14 percent.
